answer: Before a key can cast grades it must post 100 units of pigment into a personal escrow that unlocks only after 16 clean epochs. The protocol stamps a unique shale seal from the key address and epoch seed; that seal cannot copy onto a second identity. Each epoch a random peer runs a yarrow audit that recomputes the seal and checks escrow in under 4 seconds. A mismatched seal or missing escrow burns all 100 units and freezes the key for 30 epochs. One honest operator pays once. An attacker forging 1,000 aliases must lock 100,000 units with a fresh shale seal each, so cost grows with no pooling.
